subject: Q: serving deeply nested subdirs of .Rmd files?

messages.author: bff9e4feca8b059f
messages.subject: Q: serving deeply nested subdirs of .Rmd files?
parts:
I have a directory tree of independent shiny-runtime .Rmd files, and because there's no auto-indexing with directory URLs, there's an index.Rmd in each directory that auto-builds a page of links for that directory (and subdirs). However, this only works for the top level directory, all other subdirectories fail to completely load, because the relative URLs for, e.g. "shared/shiny.css" cannot be found.  In other words:

server.name:3838/top/subdir/shared/shiny.css -- exists
server.name:3838/top/subdir/subsubdir/shared/shiny.css -- not found

even though server.name/top/subdir/subsubdir/foo.Rmd does seem to trigger the shiny runtime process.

Any shiny-server config I can do to cleanly serve these URLs?

for now, I implemented a mod_rewrite rule to catch all such subsubdir/ requests, and reroute them to subdir/, but it's a fragile solution that depends on hardcoding the various "shared", "__assets__", etc.

thanks,
-Aaron

P.S. the barebones index.Rmd file I'm using in each subdir looks like this:

---

title: "Directory Listing"

runtime: shiny

output: html_document

---


## Available Pages:


```{r, echo=FALSE}

renderUI({

  pages <- dir(pattern=".Rmd$", full.names = T, recursive = T, include.dirs = T)

  pages <- sub("^\\.\\/", "", pages) # remove leading ./

  pages <- pages[pages != "index.Rmd"]

  basedir <- getwd()

  basedir <- sub("/srv/shiny-server/", "", basedir)

  links <- sprintf("http://server.name:3838/%s/%s", basedir, pages)

  pages <- sub("\\.Rmd$", "", pages)

  tags$ul(tagList(lapply(1:length(pages), function (i) { tags$li(tags$a(pages[i], href=links[i])) })))

})

```

messages.author: 3da48b33a2f506a9
messages.subject: Re: Q: serving deeply nested subdirs of .Rmd files?
parts:
Aaron,

This is currently a limitation of Shiny Server/RMarkdown; nested RMarkdown documents are not supported. We have this in our backlog to be addressed.

Regards,
Fereshteh
